title: Differential Equations for Living & Engineered Systems
description: Build, solve, and interpret first- and second-order differential equations, coupled systems, stability, and numerical integration for biological and robotic dynamics.

outcomes.description: Classify ODEs and choose solution methods.
Interpret equilibria, time constants, and stability.
Model coupled state variables as a vector system.
Check numerical solutions against physical constraints.

lesson_objectives.description: Solve separable and linear first-order ODEs.
Relate damping ratio to qualitative transient behavior.
Write a mechanical model from force balance.
Linearize a nonlinear system near an equilibrium.
Use eigenvalues to classify local stability.
Apply forward Euler and recognize its limitations.
Choose a step size based on stability and accuracy, not convenience alone.
Derive a first-order linear ODE for a well-mixed chamber from a mass balance and classify it.
Compute the steady state, the time constant and the time to reach 90% of steady state.
Apply Euler's method, compare a step with the exact solution, and use the stability limit to check a numerical result against physical constraints.
Find the equilibria of a one-variable nonlinear ODE and classify their stability from the sign of the derivative.
Interpret the linearized slope at a stable equilibrium as a recovery time constant and find the harvest rate that maximizes sustained yield.
Write two coupled compartments as a matrix system and use its eigenvalues to determine stability and the slow and fast time scales.

lessons.title: First-order models and time constants
lessons.worked_example: A sensor response with τ=4 s reaches about 63% of its final step change after 4 s and about 95% after 3τ, under the first-order model.

lessons.title: Second-order systems and mechanical response
lessons.worked_example: For m=1 kg and k=100 N/m, ωn=10 rad/s. Critical damping is ccrit=2√(km)=20 N·s/m.

lessons.title: Coupled systems, equilibria, and stability
lessons.worked_example: In a two-state linear model with J=diag(−1,−3), perturbations decay independently with time constants 1 and 1/3 time units.

lessons.title: Numerical ODEs and error control
lessons.worked_example: For ẋ=−x, x₀=1, Euler with h=0.1 gives x₁=0.9; exact x(0.1)=e^(−0.1)≈0.905, showing a small first-step error.

lessons.title: A well-mixed perfused chamber: first-order linear ODEs, steady state, time constants and a numerical check
lessons.worked_example: With D = 0.05 and k = 0.02 min⁻¹, C_ss = 7.14 mM, τ = 14.3 min and 90% is reached at 32.9 min; one Euler step of 10 min gives 5.00 mM against the exact 3.60 mM, and steps above 28.6 min diverge.

lessons.title: Equilibria and stability: harvesting a logistic population and two coupled compartments
lessons.worked_example: With r = 0.03, K = 10⁶ and h = 0.01, N* = 6.667×10⁵ cells, recovery τ = 50 h and maximum sustained yield rK/4 = 7500 cells/h; the two-compartment matrix has eigenvalues -0.0354 and -0.5646 h⁻¹, both negative, so it is stable.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (a well-mixed perfused chamber with Euler stability; equilibria and stability of a harvested population and two coupled compartments) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a common-mistakes section to 1 original lesson that lacked one (differential-equations-5); each bullet names a mistake that the lesson's own text addresses. Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in the equilibria reading. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.
There is no authored 12–15 week schedule, substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.

Practice items are short formative checks (two per prototype unit and six to seven per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 14 numerical answers in this package, nine require a unit, none checks significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
intentionally_omitted: Full instructional sequence and summative assessments are not authored yet; the original lessons extend a partial package.
